primary_reviews.rationale: This row is under-claimed rather than over-claimed. The opening at 2:30 is a genuine disjunctive clause in Hebrew — וְיוֹאָ֗ב שָׁ֚ב מֵאַחֲרֵ֣י אַבְנֵ֔ר, waw + fronted subject יואב + qatal שב — which is a stronger signal than the row's neutral phrase 'counter-movement' suggests, and it does mark the shift out of scene time. The casualty numbers verify exactly: 2:30 וַיִּפָּ֨קְד֜וּ מֵעַבְדֵ֥י דָוִ֛ד תִּשְׁעָֽה עָשָׂ֥ר אִ֖ישׁ וַעֲשָׂה אֵֽל (nineteen men and Asahel, with the niphal ויפקדו 'were mustered/missing') and 2:31 וְעַבְדֵ֣י דָוִ֗ד הִכּוּ֙ מִבִּנְיָמִ֔ן וּבְאַנְשֵׁ֖י אַבְנֵ֑ר שְׁלֹשׁ מֵא֧וֹת וְשִׁשִּׁ֛ים אִ֖ישׁ מֵֽתוּ (three hundred sixty). Note 2:31 also opens with a disjunctive וְעַבְדֵ֣י דָוִ֗ד הִכּוּ֙, so both tally clauses are off-the-line — good support for the claimed register change. The burial and the mirrored night march are literal at 2:32: וַֽיִּקְבְּרֻ֨הוּ֙ בְּקֶ֣בֶר אָבִ֔יו אֲשֶׁ֖ר בֵּ֣ית לָ֑חֶם and וַיֵּלְכ֣וּ כָל הַלַּ֗יְלָה יוֹאָב֙ וַֽאֲנָשָׁ֔יו וַיֵּאֹ֥ר לָהֶ֖ם בְּחֶבְרֽוֹן, where וַיֵּאֹ֥ר לָהֶ֖ם is the daybreak notice the row describes. Nothing marginal is claimed, so the inventory never comes into play, and 2:30-32 lies clear of the ch.19 offset range, leaving no dual reference outstanding. 'medium' is honest.

web:2Sam.2.30 confirms Joab's counter-movement and the casualty figure ('nineteen men of David's and Asahel were missing'); web:2Sam.2.31 confirms the Benjamite toll ('three hundred sixty men died'); web:2Sam.2.32 confirms Asahel's Bethlehem burial and the mirrored all-night march to Hebron at daybreak. The claimed parallel with Abner's 2:29 night march to Mahanaim is genuine (both are all-night marches closing each army's day). The rejected alternative is fair: 2:30 does shift register from confrontation to after-action accounting.

No challenge from either side; concur.

primary_reviews.rationale: The substance of the row is right but its Hebrew citation is not. The antithetic progression is genuinely disjunctive and genuinely there: 3:1 continues וְדָוִד֙ הֹלֵ֣ךְ וְחָזֵ֔ק וּבֵ֥ית שָׁא֖וּל הֹלְכִ֥ים וְדַלִּֽים — two waw + fronted-subject + participle clauses in balanced opposition, so 'David-stronger / Saul-weaker' is a real Hebrew device and not an English artifact. On the mark itself the row is accurate: pmarks_2Sam.json holds SAMEKH at 2Sam.3.1, so the setumah sits exactly at 3:1 and carries the right type, '(single-witness)' is declared, and nothing beyond corroboration is asked of it. The register contrast with 3:2 also checks out, since 3:2 opens the birth register וַיִּוָּלְד֧וּ לְדָוִ֛ד בָּנִ֖ים בְּחֶבְר֑וֹן. But the form the row quotes as its oshb evidence for the opening does not exist in the text, and the syntactic claim built on it is the reverse of what the Hebrew shows. I make no versional claim here; the reference to a cross-book campaign standard is outside this substrate and I neither confirm nor contest it.

challenges.claim: The row cites 'disjunctive והמלחמה היתה ארכה fronting at oshb:2Sam.3.1'. That string is not in 2Sam.3.1, or anywhere in the book. The verse opens וַתְּהִ֤י הַמִּלְחָמָה֙ אֲרֻכָּ֔ה בֵּ֚ין בֵּ֣ית שָׁא֔וּל וּבֵ֖ין בֵּ֣ית דָּוִ֑ד — wayyiqtol ותהי (waw-consecutive imperfect of היה) with the subject המלחמה following the verb. So the cited form is fabricated, and the syntactic claim is inverted: the opening clause is verb-initial narrative syntax, not noun-fronted disjunctive syntax. The 'Now' of the English rendering is a translator's discourse marker.
challenges.suggested_action: Replace the citation with the actual text וַתְּהִ֤י הַמִּלְחָמָה֙ אֲרֻכָּ֔ה (wayyiqtol) and move the disjunctive claim to where it is true — the two waw + subject + participle clauses וְדָוִד֙ הֹלֵ֣ךְ וְחָזֵ֔ק / וּבֵ֥ית שָׁא֖וּל הֹלְכִ֥ים וְדַלִּֽים, which alone carry the durative, off-the-line summary force the row is arguing for.

primary_reviews.rationale: web:3:1's content is confirmed ('Now there was long war between Saul's house and David's house. David grew stronger and stronger, but Saul's house grew weaker and weaker'). But the Hebrew grammar claim is wrong on two counts. First, the cited form 'והמלחמה היתה ארכה' does not match oshb:2Sam.3.1, which actually reads וַתְּהִ֤י הַמִּלְחָמָה֙ אֲרֻכָּ֔ה (verb-first: wattehi hammilchamah arukkah), not the noun-first order the citation implies. Second, and more substantively, the rationale calls this a 'disjunctive' clause, but וַתְּהִי is a wayyiqtol (vav-consecutive imperfect) form — the standard narrative-chain verb, not a disjunctive vav+noun construction. A genuinely disjunctive clause (vav + fronted noun, verbless or verb-delayed) is what correctly opens 2Sam.2.8 (וְאַבְנֵר בֶּן נֵר, verified in cluster_01/M8-2Sam-007), and 3:1 is grammatically not the same construction. The rationale's real available evidence for treating 3:1 as a self-contained durative summary is the participle+הלך idiom later in the same verse (וְדָוִד֙ הֹלֵ֣ךְ וְחָזֵ֔ק וּבֵ֥ית שָׁא֖וּל הֹלְכִ֥ים וְדַלִּֽים, an iterative/progressive construction meaning David 'kept growing' stronger while Saul's house 'kept growing' weaker), which the rationale describes correctly in English ('double antithetic progression') but does not identify by its actual grammatical mechanism, instead misattributing the effect to a nonexistent disjunctive opening. pmarks confirms SAMEKH after 3:1, correctly disclosed single-witness and weighted as weak corroboration only.

challenges.claim: boundary_rationale cites oshb:2Sam.3.1 as opening with a 'disjunctive' clause 'והמלחמה היתה ארכה', but the actual oshb text is וַתְּהִ֤י הַמִּלְחָמָה֙ אֲרֻכָּ֔ה — a wayyiqtol (vav-consecutive) verb-first narrative-chain form, not a disjunctive vav+noun construction, and the word order of the citation does not match the source text.
challenges.suggested_action: Remove the 'disjunctive...fronting' characterization and the mismatched Hebrew citation; rewrite the rationale to rest on the genuine grammatical feature present in the verse — the participle+הלך iterative construction (וְדָוִד֙ הֹלֵ֣ךְ וְחָזֵ֔ק, 'David kept growing stronger') — which does support a durative/summary reading without misnaming the syntax.

primary_reviews.rationale: This is the corrected-label case and it is now right. oshb:2Sam.3.1 verifies וַתְּהִי הַמִּלְחָמָה אֲרֻכָּה בֵּין בֵּית שָׁאוּל וּבֵין בֵּית דָּוִד, and the row explicitly declines to call that wayyiqtol disjunctive. The durative force is relocated to the genuinely disjunctive antithetic pair וְדָוִד הֹלֵךְ וְחָזֵק against וּבֵית שָׁאוּל הֹלְכִים וְדַלִּים, both verified verbatim in the same verse and both genuinely waw + subject + participle. A closed space follows MT 3:1 in the register, matching the row's typing, its single-witness caveat, and its weak framing. 'Medium' fits a one-verse span whose force rests on an intra-verse construction.

The revised rationale corrects the fabricated/mismatched citation: 3:1's actual oshb text וַתְּהִי הַמִּלְחָמָה אֲרֻכָּה is now quoted correctly and identified as wayyiqtol, not disjunctive, with the durative/summary force properly relocated to the genuinely disjunctive antithetic participial pair וְדָוִד הֹלֵךְ וְחָזֵק / וּבֵית שָׁאוּל הֹלְכִים וְדַלִּים (verified word-for-word against oshb:2Sam.3.1) -- resolving both LF-M8-2Sam-013-1 and OL-M8-2Sam-013-1. The setumah after 3:1 is verified (SAMEKH) and properly disclosed. No new defects found.

peer_crosscheck.assessment: LF-M8-2Sam-013-1 and OL-M8-2Sam-013-1 both correctly flag the same underlying defect but price it differently, and OL's higher severity is the more accurate call. I confirmed oshb:2Sam.3.1 opens וַתְּהִ֤י הַמִּלְחָמָה֙ אֲרֻכָּ֔ה — the string 'והמלחמה היתה ארכה' quoted in the boundary_rationale does not occur anywhere in the verse (different verb, different word order); this is not merely a mislabel of a real clause (as at 009/010/011) but a fabricated citation of a form the text does not contain, which is why OL's 'high' severity is correct and LF's 'medium' undersells it. Both reviewers correctly identify that the real available evidence for the durative/summary reading is the participle+הלך antithetic pair later in the same verse (וְדָוִד֙ הֹלֵ֣ךְ וְחָזֵ֔ק / וּבֵ֥ית שָׁא֖וּל הֹלְכִ֥ים וְדַלִּֽים), which is genuinely disjunctive (waw+subject+participle) and independently sufficient to ground the single-verse span. The SAMEKH mark at 3:1 is correctly disclosed single-witness and weighted weak by both. Span and confidence (medium) are unaffected; only the rationale's citation and grammatical label need replacement, per both suggested_actions (which converge). This is the book's first instance of the recurring disjunctive-mislabel class (see cluster_19 cross-cutting ruling); rule severity high per OL.

primary_reviews.rationale: This is the strongest row in the cluster and every checkable claim holds. The register opening is literal at 3:2: וַיִּוָּלְד֧וּ לְדָוִ֛ד בָּנִ֖ים בְּחֶבְר֑וֹן (ketiv וילדו / qere ויולדו). The six entries are all present with the ordinal series intact and a mother named in each: 3:2 בְכוֹרוֹ֙ אַמְנ֔וֹן לַאֲחִינֹ֖עַם הַיִּזְרְעֵאלִֽת; 3:3 וּמִשְׁנֵ֣הוּ כִלְאָ֔ב ... אשת נבל הכרמלי and וְהַשְּׁלִשִׁי֙ אַבְשָׁל֣וֹם בֶּֽן מַעֲכָ֔ה בַּת תַּלְמַ֖י מֶ֥לֶךְ גְּשֽׁוּר; 3:4 וְהָרְבִיעִ֖י אֲדֹנִיָּ֣ה בֶן חַגִּ֑ית and וְהַחֲמִישִׁ֖י שְׁפַטְיָ֥ה בֶן אֲבִיטָֽל; 3:5 וְהַשִּׁשִּׁ֣י יִתְרְעָ֔ם לְעֶגְלָ֖ה אֵ֣שֶׁת דָּוִ֑ד — six, counted, exactly as claimed. The closing frame is a true inclusio by the strict test, because both members fall on the span's own edge verses: 3:2 ...לְדָוִ֛ד בָּנִ֖ים בְּחֶבְר֑וֹן against 3:5 אֵ֛לֶּה יֻלְּד֥וּ לְדָוִ֖ד בְּחֶבְרֽוֹן, sharing ילד + לדוד + בחברון. pmarks_2Sam.json returns PE for 2Sam.3.5, so 'petuchah' is exact in type and in location alike; '(single-witness)' is stated and the mark confined to corroboration. Both edges are independently grounded by the inclusio itself, so 'high' is honestly priced.

web:2Sam.3.2 confirms the list-opening formula verbatim ('Sons were born to David in Hebron'), and the six numbered entries are confirmed with the text's own explicit ordinals: firstborn Amnon (3:2), second Chileab and third Absalom (3:3), fourth Adonijah and fifth Shephatiah (3:4), sixth Ithream (3:5) — each paired with a named mother. web:2Sam.3.5 confirms the closing inclusio verbatim ('These were born to David in Hebron'), a genuine tier-1 frame-repetition bracketing the register (3:2/3:5). Verse 3:5 does carry the pe per the mark register, the single-witness caveat is stated, and no boundary is made to rest on it. High confidence is well-justified given the exact inclusio.

peer_crosscheck.assessment: Both primaries independently verify all six register entries by the text's own ordinals and confirm a true inclusio (both members on the span's own edge verses: 3:2 ...לְדָוִ֛ד בָּנִ֖ים בְּחֶבְר֑וֹן against 3:5 אֵ֛לֶּה יֻלְּד֥וּ לְדָוִ֖ד בְּחֶבְרֽוֹן), with the PE mark at 3:5 correctly disclosed and weighted weak. primary_reviews.rationale: The oshb citation for the opening is exact: 3:6 reads וַיְהִ֗י בִּֽהְיוֹת֙ הַמִּלְחָמָ֔ה בֵּ֚ין בֵּ֣ית שָׁא֔וּל וּבֵ֖ין בֵּ֣ית דָּוִ֑ד — wayhi + bi-heyot (infinitive construct of היה with preposition), a genuine Hebrew temporal discourse frame, and the resumptive relation to 3:1 is lexically demonstrable, since 3:1 has המלחמה ... בֵּ֚ין בֵּ֣ית שָׁא֔וּל וּבֵ֖ין בֵּ֣ית דָּוִ֑ד in the same words. The 'disjunctive note' is also genuine: וְאַבְנֵ֛ר הָיָ֥ה מִתְחַזֵּ֖ק בְּבֵ֥ית שָׁאֽוּל is waw + fronted subject + היה + hitpael participle, off the narrative line, exactly as described. The oath formula in Abner's speech is real and correctly quoted: 3:9 כֹּֽה יַעֲשֶׂ֤ה אֱלֹהִים֙ לְאַבְנֵ֔ר וְכֹ֖ה יֹסִ֣יף ל֑וֹ, a tier-1 oath device. The narrator names the speaker of 3:7 only at 3:8 (וַיִּחַר֩ לְאַבְנֵ֨ר מְאֹ֜ד עַל דִּבְרֵ֣י אִֽישׁ בֹּ֗שֶׁת), so the row's attribution of the accusation to Ishbosheth is supported by the Hebrew even though 3:7 itself leaves the subject of ויאמר unexpressed. primary_reviews.rationale: Both halves of this two-verse unit verify literally. 3:26 reads וַיֵּצֵ֤א יוֹאָב֙ מֵעִ֣ם דָּוִ֔ד וַיִּשְׁלַ֤ח מַלְאָכִים֙ אַחֲרֵ֣י אַבְנֵ֔ר וַיָּשִׁ֥בוּ אֹת֖וֹ מִבּ֣וֹר הַסִּרָ֑ה וְדָוִ֖ד לֹ֥א יָדָֽע: the exit is an explicit location/participant change (מֵעִ֣ם דָּוִ֔ד), the recall is a real dispatch formula (וַיִּשְׁלַ֤ח מַלְאָכִים֙), the well of Sirah is literal (מִבּ֣וֹר הַסִּרָ֑ה), and — importantly — the exculpating note וְדָוִ֖ד לֹ֥א יָדָֽע really is a disjunctive clause (waw + fronted subject + negated qatal), so the row's one syntactic label in this row is correct, unlike several elsewhere in the book. 3:27 verifies too: וַיָּ֤שָׁב אַבְנֵר֙ חֶבְר֔וֹן וַיַּטֵּ֤הוּ יוֹאָב֙ אֶל תּ֣וֹךְ הַשַּׁ֔עַר לְדַבֵּ֥ר אִתּ֖וֹ בַּשֶּׁ֑לִי וַיַּכֵּ֤הוּ שָׁם֙ הַחֹ֔מֶשׁ וַיָּ֕מָת בְּדַ֖ם עֲשָׂה אֵ֥ל אָחִֽיו — the gate-side setting (אֶל תּ֣וֹךְ הַשַּׁ֔עַר), the blow to the belly (החמש, as at 2:23), and the blood-motive (בְּדַ֖ם עֲשָׂה אֵ֥ל אָחִֽיו) are all in the text. At the far end, 3:28's hearing formula with its temporal marker supplies the signal — וַיִּשְׁמַ֤ע דָּוִד֙ מֵאַ֣חֲרֵי כֵ֔ן. Both edges independently grounded, so 'high' is honestly priced.

web:2Sam.3.26 confirms Joab's exit and the covert recall verbatim ('When Joab had come out from David, he sent messengers after Abner, and they brought him back from the well of Sirah; but David didn't know it'). oshb:2Sam.3.26 ends וְדָוִ֖ד לֹ֥א יָדָֽע — a genuine disjunctive clause (waw + fronted subject דָוִד before the negated verb ידע), correctly characterized as an 'exculpating disjunctive,' distinguishing it from the ordinary wayyiqtol chain (contrast the misidentified case at 2Sam.3.1 in cluster_02). web:2Sam.3.27 confirms the gate-side ambush and blood-motive verbatim ('Joab took him aside into the middle of the gate to speak with him quietly, and struck him there in the body...for the blood of Asahel his brother'). The rejected alternative correctly identifies 3:28's hearing-formula ('Afterward, when David heard it') as the register shift from covert deed to public oath that closes this unit.

peer_crosscheck.assessment: Both primaries confirm Joab's exit, the covert recall to the well of Sirah, and the gate-side ambush with blood-motive at 3:27. No challenge; concur with high confidence.

The closing verdict at 3:30 is literal and is in fact a disjunctive clause the row does not claim: וְיוֹאָב֙ וַאֲבִישַׁ֣י אָחִ֔יו הָרְג֖וּ לְאַבְנֵ֑ר עַל֩ אֲשֶׁ֨ר הֵמִ֜ית אֶת עֲשָׂהאֵ֧ל אֲחִיהֶ֛ם בְּגִבְע֖וֹן בַּמִּלְחָמָֽה — waw + fronted compound subject + qatal, which is precisely the off-the-line narrator's-verdict syntax the row argues for. pmarks_2Sam.json records PE against 2Sam.3.30, so 'petuchah' names the right thing at the right verse; it is disclosed '(single-witness)' and drawn on for corroboration alone. web:2Sam.3.28 confirms the hearing formula and innocence declaration verbatim. web:2Sam.3.29 confirms a genuine five-member curse-catalogue: 'one who has a discharge, or who is a leper, or who leans on a staff, or who falls by the sword, or who lacks bread' — five items, matching oshb:2Sam.3.29's five terms (זָב, מְצֹרָע, מַחֲזִיק בַּפֶּלֶךְ, נֹפֵל בַּחֶרֶב, חֲסַר לָחֶם). web:2Sam.3.30 confirms the closing verdict verbatim, and the rationale's observation that this verse names Abishai — who was entirely absent from the 3:26-27 murder scene, which names only Joab acting alone — is textually accurate and supports treating 3:30 as a retrospective narrator verdict rather than the murder scene's epilogue. The oath at 3:35 is a genuine oath formula, כֹּ֣ה יַעֲשֶׂה לִּ֤י אֱלֹהִים֙ וְכֹ֣ה יֹסִ֔יף. Two imprecisions: the 'two-line qinah fragment' is better scanned as three lines (הַכְּמ֥וֹת נָבָ֖ל יָמ֥וּת אַבְנֵֽר / יָדֶ֣ךָ לֹֽא אֲסֻר֗וֹת וְרַגְלֶ֨יךָ֙ לֹא לִנְחֻשְׁתַּ֣יִם הֻגָּ֔שׁוּ / כִּנְפ֛וֹל לִפְנֵ֥י בְנֵֽי עַוְלָ֖ה נָפָ֑לְתָּ), which I record but do not press because colometry of unmarked Hebrew poetry is a judgment call; and the time-marker claim misstates where its evidence sits.

challenges.claim: The row describes 'the officer list in fixed office-holder formula' and glosses the entries from the English. challenges.claim: The row cites 'disjunctive וַיֵּ֧רַע הַדָּבָ֛ר at oshb:2Sam.11.27'. The words are in the text, but the form is not disjunctive: 11:27 ends וַיֵּ֧רַע הַדָּבָ֛ר אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂ֥ה דָוִ֖ד בְּעֵינֵ֥י יְהוָֽה — וַיֵּרַע is a waw-consecutive imperfect (wayyiqtol) of r-'-', verb-initial, with the subject הַדָּבָר following it; there is no waw + fronted constituent. The adversative force the row hears ('But the thing … displeased Yahweh') comes from the WEB rendering, not from Hebrew syntax. This is the same mislabel as at oshb:2Sam.3.1 (וַתְּהִ֤י הַמִּלְחָמָה֙ אֲרֻכָּ֔ה), so it looks like a systematic reading of English word order as Hebrew fronting.
challenges.suggested_action: Relabel as a clause-final evaluative wayyiqtol (וַיֵּ֧רַע הַדָּבָ֛ר … בעיני יהוה) — its force comes from position and from the lexical reversal of David's own אַל יֵרַ֤ע בְּעֵינֶ֨יךָ֙ at 11:25, not from disjunctive syntax; keep the oshb citation but drop 'disjunctive'.

This is the same category of error flagged at 2Sam.3.1 in cluster_02 (also a wayyiqtol mislabeled 'disjunctive'): a genuinely disjunctive clause fronts a noun before the verb (as at 2Sam.3.26's וְדָוִד לֹא יָדָע, correctly identified in cluster_03), and 11:27 does not have that structure. The diagnostic question verifies at 13:4 and the scheme speech at 13:5, which does dictate the request in direct speech (וְאָמַרְתָּ֣ אֵלָ֡יו תָּ֣בֹא נָא֩ תָמָ֨ר אֲחוֹתִ֜י וְתַבְרֵ֣נִי לֶ֗חֶם). However, the rationale's opening claim — that 21:7 is 'a disjunctive exception notice' — is wrong: oshb:2Sam.21.7 opens וַיַּחְמֹל הַמֶּלֶךְ עַל מְפִיבֹשֶׁת, and וַיַּחְמֹל is a wayyiqtol (vav-consecutive imperfect, Qal of חמל 'to spare') — the standard verb-first narrative-chain form, not a disjunctive vav+noun construction. This is now the fifth confirmed instance of the same mislabeling pattern in this book (2Sam.3.1; 2Sam.11.27; 2Sam.12.26; 2Sam.13.34).
